title: Clean Code Examples
description: Small Clean Code examples from the lessons. Each example links back to its explanation and practice task.

examples.title: Write for the next reader
examples.description: Code is read many times. A clear name explains the purpose of a value without making the reader solve a puzzle.

examples.title: Name actions with verbs
examples.description: Function names should explain what the action does. A reader should not need to inspect every line to understand a call.
examples.code:
function addPrices(first, second) { return first + second; }
console.log(addPrices(3, 4));

examples.title: Keep one job in a function
examples.description: A small function with one clear job is easier to test and reuse. Separate a calculation from drawing a page.
examples.code:
const totalPrice = prices => prices.reduce((sum, price) => sum + price, 0);
console.log(totalPrice([2, 3]));

examples.title: Replace unexplained numbers
examples.description: A named constant explains why a special value appears. It also gives the rule one clear place to change.

examples.title: Return early for simple cases
examples.description: A guard clause handles a special case early. It can reduce deep nesting and make the main path easier to follow.

examples.title: Avoid needless repeated rules
examples.description: When the same rule appears in several places, changes can be missed. Put a shared rule in one clear function.
examples.code:
const passes = score => score >= 5;
console.log(passes(4), passes(7));

examples.title: Comments explain reasons
examples.description: A useful comment explains why a choice was made. The code should already explain ordinary steps through names.

examples.title: Make errors helpful
examples.description: An error should say what input was wrong or what action failed. It should not expose private details.

examples.title: Prefer clear conditions
examples.description: A condition is easier to read when it states one clear question. Name a complicated condition if its purpose is not obvious.

examples.title: Avoid surprising changes
examples.description: A function that returns a new value can be easier to reason about than one that changes its input. Make changes clear in the function name or contract.

examples.title: Refactor without changing behaviour
examples.description: Refactoring improves the code structure while keeping the same intended behaviour. Tests help check that the behaviour stayed the same.

examples.title: Review a small change
examples.description: A focused review checks whether a change solves its stated problem and keeps the code readable. Small changes are easier to inspect.
examples.code:
const trimTitle = title => title.trim();
console.log(trimTitle("  Moon  ") === "Moon");
